response.name: PAN-OS Allowed Inbound Administrative Access
response.description: Detects allowed network access from an external source to an internal system on an administrative service port. This shows that the firewall allowed the network connection; it does not prove that someone logged in, used the service, or compromised the destination.
response.note:
## What this alert means

An external system was allowed to connect to an internal system using an administrative service such as SSH, RDP, SMB, or another management protocol. This may be approved VPN or vendor access, but it should be checked.

## What to check

Review the source address, destination address, destination port, time, firewall action, and the firewall rule that allowed the connection. Confirm whether the source is an approved VPN, vendor, or other authorised service. Identify the owner of the destination system and check its host authentication logs for a successful login or other related activity.

## Response

Do not automatically block, isolate, reset passwords, or disable accounts based on this alert alone. If the access is not authorised or successful access cannot be explained, preserve the relevant logs, contact the system owner, and escalate through the approved incident-response process.
response.query: event.dataset:"panw.panos" and panw.panos.type:"TRAFFIC" and panw.panos.action:allow and event.action:flow_started and destination.port:(22 or 23 or 135 or 139 or 445 or 3389 or 5985 or 5986) and not source.ip:(10.0.0.0/8 or 172.16.0.0/12 or 192.168.0.0/16) and destination.ip:(10.0.0.0/8 or 172.16.0.0/12 or 192.168.0.0/16)
